whatItIs.text: A light savoury liquid simmered from vegetables and aromatics — the French mirepoix of onion, carrot, and celery plus whatever the kitchen has to spare.

historyNote.text: Stock technique is older than any written recipe: classical French kitchens flavour stocks with a bouquet garni of parsley, bay, and thyme, and cooks have always used the 'less desirable' vegetable trimmings — carrot skins, celery cores — that get strained away anyway.

howToChoose.text: Low-sodium gives you control; check labels for real vegetables rather than flavourings, and avoid powders that list salt first.

storage.text: Opened cartons and homemade stock keep covered in the fridge; freeze the rest soon after opening.

useItUp.text: Freeze in cubes for cooking rice and deglazing pans; a cup of leftover stock plus leftovers and noodles is a 10-minute soup.

substitutions.note: richer body; fine unless cooking vegetarian

substitutions.substitute: water + a spoon of miso or soy
